feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 8 (y=0.07 m, ±0.065 m, 16 mm, 56.40) gave s-bend line loss of 0.05 per run and s-bend progress of 0.1825, but slalom still lost the line once per run, with max_error 0.0604 m and oscillation 0.131. Iteration 7 (y=0.065 m, ±0.065 m, 35.77) lost the slalom line again and dropped s-bend progress to 0.04. So the lead below 0.067 m is risky, and 0.067 m is a small step rather than a fall-back. Iteration 6 (wheel_radius 0.04 m) showed that more speed brings line loss back, so speed stays at 0.03 m. Slalom oscillation stayed at 0.13 to 0.14 at every row tested (iterations 3 to 8), so it is not lead-driven. The oval has been fixed at progress 0.115 and max_error about 0.061 m since iteration 1. What I compensated for: kp 2.0, kd 0.10, ki 0 and the [-2,-1,0,1,2] weights were kept, because the signal stays within about ±2 across the ±0.065 m spread. Next race: if slalom line_loss_events is 0 and max_error is below 0.06 m, keep the ±0.065 m spread and the 0.067 m row. If slalom line loss returns at 0.067 m, the spread is not the cure. Then keep the spread and do not move the row further forward or back. If slalom max_error is still at or above 0.06 m with zero line loss, widen the spread to ±0.08 m with 16 mm footprints.

If slalom max_error is still at or above 0.06 m with zero line loss (iteration 8 gave 0.0604 m, iteration 7 gave 0.0642 m), widen sensor x to ±0.08 m with 16 mm footprints, so the line stays under the sensors at the largest bend offsets.

If the score is at or above 56.4 with zero line loss, keep the geometry fixed and test sensor_size 0.012 m at the same positions, to check whether a smaller footprint reduces the jitter that the 16 mm footprint may add (iteration 1 showed the 16 mm footprint removed line loss).
